Simon Hjerrild is a prominent figure in Danish psychiatry, serving as a chief physician (*overlæge*) and clinical lecturer with a PhD. He is best known in the context of national quality assurance as the chair (*forperson*) of the steering committee for the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]] [^src2]. His professional authority in ADHD diagnostics and treatment is central to the oversight of psychiatric care quality in Denmark.

In his clinical and academic roles, Hjerrild is affiliated with the [[bua|Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Afdeling (BUA)]] and the [[aarhus-universitetshospital-psykiatrien|Aarhus Universitetshospital, Psykiatrien]], specifically working within Team for ADHD, clinic 2, in the psychosis department [^src1] [^src2] [^src3]. He is also associated with [[dps-midtjylland|DPS Midtjylland]] (the Central Denmark Region branch of the Danish Psychiatric Society) [^src2] [^src3]. 

Hjerrild's leadership on the ADHD database steering committee places him at the forefront of evaluating and improving ADHD treatment across Denmark. The database's annual reports for 2023 and 2024, which he helps oversee, represent critical evaluations of the healthcare system's ability to meet national quality indicators. These reports highlight systemic challenges such as rising wait times, low target fulfillment, and registration deficiencies, while also marking a historic expansion in 2024 to include complete measurements for both children, youths, and adults across public and private sectors. As chair, Hjerrild plays a vital role in guiding the technical and organizational aspects of data collection, including the clinical validation of data and the implementation of process markers to ensure accurate quality monitoring in Danish ADHD care [^src1] [^src2] [^src3].
